name: Centipede, Tyrant
body:
Tyrant Centipede
CR 23

XP 819,200
N Colossal magical beast
Init +4; Senses blindsight 60 ft., low-light vision, see in darkness, tremorsense 300 ft.; Perception +36; Aura antimagic field (30 ft.)

DEFENSE

AC 37, touch 7, flat-footed 32 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +30 natural, -8 size)
hp 555 (30d10+390)
Fort +29, Ref +21, Will +16
DR 10/epic; Immune acid, mind-affecting, poison; Resist fire 30, electricity 20, sonic 20; SR 34

OFFENSE

Speed 60 ft., burrow 30 ft., climb 60 ft.
Melee bite +41 (8d10+36/19-20/x4 plus grab and poison)
Space 30 ft.; Reach 30 ft.
Special Attacks constrict (8d10+36), rend armor

STATISTICS

Str 46, Dex 19, Con 34, Int 5, Wis 19, Cha 10
Base Atk +30; CMB +56 (+60 grapple and sunder); CMD 73 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Cornugon Smash, Critical Focus, Dodge, Greater Sunder, Greater Vital Strike, Improved Critical (bite), Improved Sunder, Improved Vital Strike, Iron Will, Power Attack, Staggering Critical, Stunning Critical, Toughness, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Climb +30, Perception +36
Languages Aklo (can’t speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poison (Ex)

Bite–injury; save Fortitude DC 37; frequency 1/round for 10 rounds; effect 1d6 Dex drain; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Ruinous Mandibles (Ex)

The bite attack of the tyrant centipede adds double its Strength bonus to damage, ignores damage reduction and deals quadruple damage on a critical hit.

Rend Armor (Ex)

If a tyrant centipede grapples an opponent wearing armor, it chews away the armor with its powerful mandibles. With a successful grapple check it gets a free sunder attempt targeting the opponent’s armor and ignoring its hardness.

ECOLOGY

Environment underground
Organization solitary Treasure incidental

Thankfully rare, tyrant centipedes are apex predators of the bowels of the world. In a realm of powerful, magic-wielding civilizations and monstrous, eldritch beings, those creatures distinguish themselves by not simply being resistant to magic themselves, but somehow erasing any and all magic near them. This ability, combined with their overwhelming strength and size, allows them to hunt, destroy and devour with impunity, as creatures able to defeat those beings on their own grounds are very rare indeed. Tyrant centipedes are always solitary and dwell deep beneath the ground, deeper than any drow and duergar live, gnawing on the very foundations of the world. Mu spores, bholes, neothelid overlords and some of the oldest underground dragons are about the only native creatures that can stand against a tyrant centipede in open combat. Such duels don’t happen frequently, as tyrant centipedes are both rare and extremely territorial. When they see an invader of some sort in a vast stretch of underground that they consider theirs, they set out immediately to confront the enemy and never back down until they or their opponent is dead, which makes any rematches unlikely.

Tyrant centipedes rarely wander above their deep lairs. Most often they aim to kill some sort of large prey and then lower their activity, digesting their meal and saving energy only to set out on a next, big hunt a few months later. If the region is somehow abundant in creatures large enough to satiate a tyrant centipede, it hunts, kills and eats much more frequently, often depopulating the area in quite a rapid fashion. If the prey is scarce, though, it isn’t unheard of tyrant centipedes traveling to higher levels of the underground and even assaulting communities of beings that live there, their greatest magic and weapons as nothing beneath the centipede’s might and all the brave mages and warriors reduced to bites destined to sate the beast’s hunger. Occasionally, some savage underground creatures begin to worship the centipede, believing it to be a vengeful deity sent to slaughter their magic-wielding oppressors. Of course, the centipede doesn’t care for its newfound believers, devouring them as eagerly as it does their foes.
